newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA OVERTURNS JAIL TERM IN ILIESCU KGB CASE.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA OVERTURNS JAIL TERM IN ILIESCU KGB CASE.

text.p: Romania's ex-president Ion Iliescu will not challenge the overturning of a jail sentence handed down to two journalists for alleging that he had been recruited by the ex-Soviet KGB, a party colleague said on Tuesday.
"Iliescu will take no action against the ruling," former foreign minister Teodor Melescanu, now a spokesman of Iliescu's leftist Party of Social Democracy, told Reuters.
"The prosecutors started this trial and it is up to them to do what they consider appropriate."

The Bucharest municipal court on Monday quashed a one-year sentence imposed last October on the director general of the daily Ziua, Sorin Rosca Stanescu, for "defaming state authority". His reporter, Tana Ardeleanu, had got 14 months.
The panel of judges gave no reason for overturning the district court sentence. Prosecutors have 10 days to appeal.

In 1995, the two accused ran a series of stories on Iliescu alleging he had been recruited by the now-defunct KGB secret service while a student in Moscow in the early 1950s. Iliescu has denied the allegations.

The reports also held Iliescu "morally responsible" for more than 1,000 deaths during the December 1989 uprising which toppled communism. Two-thirds of the victims died after Ceausescu fled Bucharest in a helicopter on December 22.

Iliescu, a communist official who served in a variety of positions under Ceausescu, emerged from the turmoil as president and remained in office until he was defeated in last November's election by reformist Emil Constantinescu.
The two journalists had been charged with "grave insults to the institution of the presidency through forged documents" under a libel law criticised by many lawyers as vague.

Stanescu described Tuesday's ruling as "the first normal one in the trial" but said he had no reason to celebrate. He said the presiding judge had not allowed defence lawyers to produce witnesses and disregarded documents they had submitted.
"My disappointment is that the trial hasn't solved the basic issue. Was Iliescu recruited by the KGB or not?" he said.
